newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says France set on Rafale fighter.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says France set on Rafale fighter.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac pledged on Friday that France would stick to its commitments on military procurement including the Rafale fighterbomber and Europe's planned Future Large Aircraft (FLA).

A spokesman quoted Chirac as telling staff at the Avord airforce base that the defence budget law "solemnly reaffirmed the necessity and the future of Rafale" and added that he was convinced Europeans would build the FLA transport plane.
"I know that some people are raising doubts over the government's ability to honour and respect the commitments which have been made," Chirac was quoted as saying.
"On the defence budget, we cannot afford any going back nor any hesitation. Whatever the rigours of time, the decisions which have been made will not be cast in doubt," he said.

Cuts in the six-year defence budget have forced combat plane maker Dassault to examine novel methods of financing the Rafale programme as only two planes have been ordered by the air force for 1999, a number it deems insufficient for winning export orders.

Some 15 other planes would be ordered later to form a squadron in the year 2005. The law also provides for the order of 16 "Navy" Rafales to equip the new Charles-de-Gaulle aircraft carrier in the year 2000.

State-owned aerospace group Aerospatiale has suggested building the FLA jointly with seven other European partners but since France dropped development funding, the company has been looking at commercial funding for the project.
